title: OLIVE LEAVES AS A LOW-COST ADSORBENT FOR PHENOL REMOVAL FROM AQUEOUS SOLUTIONS

OLIVE LEAVES AS A LOW-COST ADSORBENT FOR PHENOL REMOVAL FROM AQUEOUS SOLUTIONS

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Seroor Atalah Khaleefa Ali
Print ISSN : 2523-5664
Online ISSN : 2523-5672

Doi: 10.26480/wcm.03.2026.544.553

ABSTRACT

This investigation sought to assess the potential of employing olive leaves as a low-cost and eco-friendly adsorbent for the remediation of phenol from aqueous solutions. The adsorption behavior was evaluated by batch experiments at different operational conditions, including contact time, initial phenol concentration, solution temperature, pH, adsorbent dosage, and agitation rate. The design factors were evaluated within the ranges of 5–180 min, 1–50 mg/L, 25–50 °C, pH 1–10, 0.5–7.0 g, and 100–500 rpm, respectively. The results demonstrated that phenol remediation declined with raising initial concentration of phenol and temperature of solution, while it increased with raising contact time, adsorbent dosage, and agitation speed. The effect of pH was governed by the conditions of solution, exhibiting improved phenol removal at acidic conditions, followed by an increasing at the basic media. The optimal factors were 150 min of contact time, 6.5 g of olive leaves, pH 5, ambient temperature, and an agitation speed of 350 rpm, achieved 75.217% as a maximum removal efficiency of phenol from an initial concentration of 48 mg/L.
